concepts.title: Etymology and Concept of Yoga
concepts.definition: Yoga originates from the Sanskrit root 'Yuj', signifying connection, yoking, or integration of individual self-awareness with higher universal consciousness.
concepts.key_idea: Achieving unified consciousness and balance between physical existence and mental state.
question_patterns: what is the etymology of the word yoga
explain the meaning of the sanskrit root yuj
how is yoga defined in ancient scriptures
what does yoga signify beyond physical exercise
Explain etymology and concept of yoga in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Trace the term to Sanskrit root 'Yuj' meaning to join, yoke, or unite.
Describe it as the alignment of individual consciousness with universal consciousness.
Clarify that physical postures are only one aspect of a complete holistic life philosophy.

concepts.title: Historical Epochs of Yoga
concepts.definition: The historical evolution of yogic philosophy structured across six major ages, spanning over 5000 years from ancient seals to contemporary worldwide recognition.
concepts.formula: History = Pre-Vedic + Vedic/Upanishadic + Classical + Post-Classical + Modern + Contemporary
concepts.key_idea: Systematic transition of yogic practices from early civilization seals to international wellness adoption.
question_patterns: trace the historical development of yoga
what are the main historical periods of yoga
describe the significance of the classical period in yoga
how did yoga evolve from pre-vedic times to the modern era
Explain historical epochs of yoga in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Outline the phases: Pre-Vedic, Vedic & Upanishadic, Classical, Post-Classical, Modern, and Contemporary.
Identify archaeological evidence like the Pashupati seal, Patanjali's Yoga Sutras, and the UN General Assembly declaring June 21st as International Day of Yoga.

concepts.title: Astanga Yoga (Eight Limbs)
concepts.definition: A comprehensive eight-stage framework designed by Maharshi Patanjali to regulate mental fluctuations and achieve complete spiritual absorption.
concepts.formula: Astanga = Yama + Niyama + Asana + Pranayama + Pratyahara + Dharana + Dhyana + Samadhi
concepts.key_idea: Sequential progression from social ethics and personal purity to internal meditative absorption.
question_patterns: list the eight limbs of patanjali yoga
explain astanga yoga and its components
what is the difference between yama and niyama
how do the eight limbs lead to samadhi
Explain astanga yoga (eight limbs) in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Detail Yama (social ethics), Niyama (personal observances), Asana (postures), and Pranayama (breath regulation).
Detail Pratyahara (withdrawal of senses), Dharana (concentration), Dhyana (meditation), and Samadhi (spiritual absorption).

concepts.title: Panchamahavrata and Eightfold Path
concepts.definition: Ethical codes established by Mahavira (Five Great Vows) and Buddha (Eightfold Path) that served as early spiritual guidelines integral to yogic sadhana.
concepts.formula: Ethical Practice = Panchamahavrata (Jain Vows) + Atthangika Magga (Buddhist Path)
concepts.key_idea: Moral restraint and balanced cognitive conduct form the bedrock of self-discipline in yoga.
question_patterns: what are the panchamahavrata of mahavira
list the eightfold path of buddha
how do jain and buddhist ethical principles relate to yoga sadhana
explain the five great vows in jainism
Explain panchamahavrata and eightfold path in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Enumerate Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Aparigraha (renunciation/non-possession), Asteya (non-stealing), and Brahmacharya (celibacy).
Enumerate Right Understanding, Right Thought, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, and Right Concentration.

concepts.title: Traditional Schools of Yoga
concepts.definition: Distinct philosophical streams and lineages that provide specialized pathways toward self-realization suited to different human temperaments.
concepts.formula: Yoga Schools = Jnana + Bhakti + Karma + Patanjala + Hatha
concepts.key_idea: Multiple complementary paths catering to intellect, devotion, selfless work, mental discipline, and body-energy balance.
question_patterns: what are the main traditional schools of yoga
compare jnana yoga bhakti yoga and karma yoga
explain the philosophy behind hatha yoga
what is the main objective of patanjala yoga
Explain traditional schools of yoga in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Categorize Jnana (path of knowledge/wisdom), Bhakti (path of devotion), Karma (path of selfless action), Patanjala (mind regulation), and Hatha (physical-energetic balance).
Describe how each path targets a unique dimension of human personality to overcome ignorance and suffering.

concepts.title: Three Stages of Jnana Yoga
concepts.definition: A triadic method of intellectual inquiry consisting of listening to truth, logical reflection, and deep meditative assimilation.
concepts.key_idea: Transforming theoretical wisdom into direct realization through reflection and sustained meditation.
question_patterns: what are the three stages of jnana yoga
explain sravana manana and nididhyasana
how does a practitioner attain knowledge in jnana yoga
describe the process of intellectual self-inquiry in yoga
Explain three stages of jnana yoga in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Absorbing and listening attentively to scriptural teachings and instructions.
Reflecting and contemplating rationally upon instructions to establish intellectual conviction.
Engaging in profound, unbroken meditation to internalize truth and achieve oneness with reality.

concepts.title: Navadha Bhakti (Ninefold Devotion)
concepts.definition: Nine progressive devotional practices designed to direct emotions toward the divine and dissolve egoistic barriers.
concepts.key_idea: Refinement of human emotions through nine distinct devotional expressions.
question_patterns: what is navadha bhakti
list the nine forms of devotional service in bhakti yoga
how does bhakti yoga purify human emotions
explain the practice of kirtana and smarana
Explain navadha bhakti (ninefold devotion) in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: List Sravana (listening), Kirtana (praising/singing), Smarana (remembering), Pada-sevana (service), Arcana (worship), Vandana (paying homage), Dasya (servitude), Sakhya (friendship), and Atma-nivedana (self-surrender).
Describe how devotional engagement removes jealousy, anger, and pride while instilling bliss and inner peace.

concepts.title: Panchakosha (Five Sheaths of Existence)
concepts.definition: The Taittiriya Upanishad model describing human existence across five concentric sheaths from outer physical matter to inner bliss.
concepts.formula: Existence = Annamaya + Pranamaya + Manomaya + Vijnanamaya + Anandamaya
concepts.key_idea: Multi-layered framework connecting physical structure, energetic force, mental thoughts, higher wisdom, and pure bliss.
question_patterns: describe the panchakosha framework
what are the five sheaths of human body according to taittiriya upanishad
explain the difference between annamaya kosha and pranamaya kosha
which kosha represents the bliss body
Explain panchakosha (five sheaths of existence) in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Annamaya (food sheath) forms the physical body; Pranamaya (energy sheath), Manomaya (mental sheath), and Vijnanamaya (wisdom sheath) form the subtle body.
Anandamaya (bliss sheath) forms the causal body closest to the ultimate self.

concepts.title: Yoga for Holistic Health
concepts.definition: A comprehensive healthcare framework that establishes harmony across physical, cognitive, emotional, social, and spiritual dimensions.
concepts.formula: Holistic Health = Physical + Cognitive + Emotional + Social + Spiritual Wellbeing
concepts.key_idea: Treating root causes of disease to maintain internal equilibrium (homeostasis) and mental calmness.
question_patterns: how does yoga promote holistic health
explain the impact of yoga on cognitive and emotional development
what is the role of yamas and niyamas in social health
how do yogic practices restore bodily homeostasis
Explain yoga for holistic health in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Asanas and Kriyas tune physiological systems and clear toxins; Pranayama and Dhyana enhance focus, memory, and stress control.

solution_steps.action: explain emotional, social, and spiritual benefits
solution_steps.explain: Bhakti Yoga stabilizes mood; Yamas/Niyamas cultivate moral character and healthy interpersonal relationships.

concepts.title: Categories of Yogic Practices
concepts.definition: A structured system of practical techniques including detoxification, body alignments, breath regulation, energy control, and silent meditation.
concepts.formula: Practices = Kriya + Surya Namaskara + Asana + Pranayama + Bandha/Mudra + Dhyana
concepts.key_idea: A versatile toolkit of mental and physical disciplines designed for personal wellness and self-realization.
question_patterns: what are the major categories of practical yoga techniques
explain the purpose of kriya and surya namaskara
what are bandhas and mudras in pranayama
classify asanas based on body postures
Explain categories of yogic practices in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Kriyas (cleansing procedures), Surya Namaskara (12-pose sequence), and Asanas (standing, sitting, prone, and supine postures).
Pranayama (breath control), Bandhas/Mudras (locks and subtle gestures), and Dhyana (meditation).

worked_examples.question_pattern: Explain the three sequential stages of Jñāna Yoga and how they lead to self-realization.

solution_template.explain: First step is Sravana, which means listening to and absorbing teachings from scriptures and teachers.
Second step is Manana, which involves deep contemplation and intellectual reasoning to clarify doubts.
Third step is Nididhyasana, sustained meditative assimilation of truth to experience oneness with reality.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Outline the five sheaths (Pancakoṣas) of human existence and map them to the gross, subtle, and causal bodies.

solution_template.explain: Annamaya Kosha (food sheath) forms the gross physical body (Sthula Sarira).
Pranamaya (vital energy), Manomaya (mind/emotions), and Vijnanamaya (higher intellect) form the subtle body (Suksma Sarira).
Anandamaya Kosha (bliss sheath) corresponds to the causal body (Karana Sarira).
